passages.title: The Psychology of Habit Formation
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of psychology, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: A cue such as a time or place can prompt a familiar behaviour. A very small first step can make a new routine easier to begin.
Repeating an action in a stable context can make it more automatic. Motivation changes from day to day and cannot always be relied upon.
Recording behaviour can reveal patterns that are otherwise easy to overlook. Missing a day does not automatically prevent a routine from becoming established.
Changing the environment can make a desired action easier to perform. Some behaviours become automatic more quickly than others.

paras: Ocean currents move heat between different regions of the planet. Winds are an important driver of many surface currents.
Salt content influences the density of seawater. Deep ocean circulation can take a very long time to complete.
Ocean circulation influences the conditions experienced by coastal organisms. Researchers use ships, buoys, satellites and other systems to observe currents.
Computer models investigate how circulation might change. Changes in circulation can have different effects in different regions.

passages.title: The Economics of Public Libraries
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of economics, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Libraries often provide digital access, study space and community programmes. Many library benefits do not have a direct market price.
Access to computers and online resources can help people who lack them at home. People's ability to use libraries depends partly on when they are open.
Different neighbourhoods may need different services from their libraries. Evaluations may combine borrowing data, surveys and other indicators.
Money spent on one service cannot be spent on another possible use. Partnerships with local organisations can help libraries reach more residents.
